The committed `Layout` class has no such method and the committed `DefineParser._int` substitutes only `lay.limb_off(..)`.  ADAPTER: `BlockLayout` (a subclass) adds `limb_off_m` with exactly layout.rs's arithmetic, and `BlockDefineParser._int` substitutes `lay.limb_off_m(k)` with it before delegating.  No value is assumed: the plane index comes from the parsed consts and `t_pad` from the toy profile B-7 derives.  [PIN re-read 2026-09-20 after the shape generalisation: layout.rs:647 -> :1149-1151, argument.rs:570 -> :935; the arithmetic is the same at the toy, where `ids.at` is the identity and `t_pad == T`.]

The shape generalisation replaced every one of those calls with `sh.helpers(Dom::D)`, which returns the COUNT alone and is rewritten by B-9 instead; `lay.helpers(` occurs zero times in private_block/argument.rs.  `adapters_used` no longer reports B-2, and that is the evidence for this line.]

B-3  `let <name> = if <cond> { <challenge> } else { <point>.clone() }` -- private_block/argument.rs:1084, `let r_row = if slot == SC_DMM { tr.challenge_fp2_vec(lt) } else { pts.r_tf.clone() };`, the one construct the feed-forward matmul arm needs and the accepted source never uses (the committed parser handles only the TUPLE form `let (a, b) = if flag {..} else {..}` and only with a bool local as the condition).  ADAPTER: `BlockDefineParser._statement` evaluates the condition with the committed `_cond`, takes the live branch and binds a challenge vector or a `pts.X` / `pts.X.clone()` vector; anything else falls through to the committed parser unchanged.  The bound symbols are `SC_DMM.r_row[i]` (the Rust local's own name), distinct from `SC_GMM.r_tf[i]`, which is what the PCS grouping keys on.

B-4  `protocol.rs::logup_sum_claim` indirections -- the accepted source loops `for p in 0..N_H` and signs with `if p == H_GU8 || p == H_GEXP`; the block (private_block/protocol.rs:143-144) loops `for p in lay.h_planes()` and signs with `if hids.is_table(p)`.  The committed `parse_logup_sum` refuses the first and silently reads an EMPTY negated set from the second.  ADAPTER: `normalise_logup_source` resolves BOTH indirections out of layout.rs itself and rewrites those two lines into the spelling the committed parser understands, so that all of its own assertions (`point: vec![]`, `value: Fp2::ZERO`, loop range == N_H) still run.  Both forms are asserted, not assumed; an unexpected body is a hard parse error.  [PINS re-read 2026-09-20 after the shape generalisation.  protocol.rs:54-55 -> :143-144.  `fn h_planes` read `(0..N_H).collect()` at layout.rs:615-617 and now reads `(0..self.hids.n_h()).collect()` at :1117-1119, so the loop bound is taken as `N_H` on the strength of `Layout::new`'s own freeze gate `assert_eq!(lay.hids.n_h(), N_H, ..)` (layout.rs:985), which this adapter requires to be present and which grow_tests.rs:858 asserts again on `HIds::new(&Shape::toy())`.  The sign test moved from the free `h_is_table(p)` to the shape-driven `hids.is_table(p)`, whose body must read `(self.gu8..self.gu8 + 3).contains(&plane)` (layout.rs:549-551); the three PLANE NAMES are still read out of `fn h_is_table`'s `matches!(plane, ...)`, which survives at layout.rs:437-439, and grow_tests.rs:872 asserts the two agree on every plane at the toy.]

B-5  the two OWED negative controls re-use the committed rank tool with its accepted rebinding: after `INV.run_rank_tool` returns, the already-rebound module instance is taken from `sys.modules['zk60_attention_pair_schedule']` and its own `build_schedule` / `a_model_groups(share_mask=...)` / `build_model` / `analyze_fast` are called again.  No constant is rebound a second time and no tool function is redefined.

B-6  the activation table's lookup total.  The committed `lookup_total` knows two tables (U8 by summing `lookups(dom)` over `LOOKUP_DOMS`, exp as `1 << Dom::S.log()`).  The block has a third, the activation table (private_block/argument.rs:1216 `f_act`, one lookup per `Dom::F` element).  `block_lookup_totals` adds `act = 1 << Dom::F.log()` by exactly the committed tool's own convention for exp.  The U8 and exp totals are the committed function's, unchanged.  [PIN re-read 2026-09-20: argument.rs:766 -> :1216.]

B-7  `Dom::log` no longer HOLDS the domain logs (step S6).  layout.rs:160-162 delegates to `domain_log_at(self.natural_log(), self.carries_h_planes(), LOG_N)`, and the committed `parse_dom_logs` reads a `match` that is no longer there -- this is the immediate cause of the nine errors finding S9-F6 reported.  ADAPTER: `normalise_layout_source` requires `Dom::log`'s body to be EXACTLY that call and `domain_log_at`'s body (layout.rs:136-142) to be exactly the ruling-P-3 lift `if carries_h_planes && natural < log_n { log_n } else { natural }`; it then runs the COMMITTED arm parser on `natural_log`'s own match (layout.rs:146-155), reads the domains that carry no H plane out of `carries_h_planes`'s `!matches!(self, ..)` (layout.rs:157-159) and `LOG_N` out of the consts, applies the lift in Python and rewrites `Dom::log`'s body into the literal match the committed parser reads.  At the toy the lift moves nothing (`lifted_by_P3` is empty) and the nine logs are the nine the accepted run recorded.  The same function derives the TOY PROFILE that adapters B-1 and B-9 need -- the six axis logs, inverted from the nine natural logs by `shape.rs:390-404`'s rule, and the three byte-limb counts, by `shape.rs:372-386`'s rule on layout.rs's own `NORM_WRHO` / `WRHO_S` / `F_P`.  Ten cross-checks travel with it, and any of them failing is a hard parse error, not a warning: the three domains the inversion does not consume, the six frozen toy geometry constants `T` / `D` / `H` / `DH` / `F` / `KV`, which no longer drive anything in layout.rs and are now only a witness, and the pinned `LN_TOY` / `LS_TOY` / `LP_TOY` (layout.rs:281-283).

B-8  `lookups(dom)` is now `lookups_at(&Shape::toy(), &Ids::toy(), dom)` (layout.rs:643-645), whose match arms are written over the shape: `(0..ln).map(..)` for a limb group and `if norm_top { .. }` for correction C-6's four droppable `scaled` lookups.  The committed `parse_lookup_counts` handles neither.  ADAPTER: `normalise_layout_source` requires `lookups`'s body to be exactly that call and `lookups_at` (layout.rs:667-742) to bind `let (ln, ls, lp) = (ids.ln, ids.ls, ids.lp);` and `let norm_top = !sh.norm_top_is_full_byte();`, substitutes the TOY's `ln` / `ls` / `lp` and resolves the `if norm_top` blocks (true at the toy, `NORM_WRHO = 29` against `8 * 4`), then hands the result to the COMMITTED counter, which still does all the counting (`v.push` = 1, `v.extend([..])` = the list's length, `sym(..)` = 2, `(0..k).map(..)` = k). An `else` branch or an unknown condition appearing in `lookups_at` is a hard parse error.

B-9  the shaped spellings inside `argument::define`.  Nine kinds of expression changed their spelling without changing their value at the toy, and `normalise_define_source` rewrites each one, inside `define`'s body alone, into the spelling the committed `DefineParser` already reads: `ids.at(P)` -> `P` and `ids.nr(k)`..`ids.sg(k)` -> their toy base plus `k` (the toy's id map is the identity -- `Layout::new`'s freeze gate, layout.rs:987, `assert!((0..N_A).all(|p| lay.ids.at(p) == p))`); `hids.first_helper(D)`, `hids.helper(D, j)`, `hids.sexp()`, `hids.fact()`, `hids.u()` and `hids.table_helpers()` -> the literal helper planes of `fn helpers` and the `H_*` constants, which grow_tests.rs:855-877 asserts one by one on `HIds::new(&Shape::toy())`; `sh.helpers(D)` -> `helpers(D).1`; `sh.log(D)` -> `D.log()`; `sh.size(D)` -> `1 << D.log()`; `sh.limbs_*()` and the six `sh.<axis>` fields -> the toy profile's values; and `lg(v)` -> `v.trailing_zeros()` (argument.rs:592-595).  Four small evaluator extensions go with it, all of them forms the accepted source never uses: `helpers(D).0` (the FIRST helper plane; the committed `_int` substitutes only the pair's second member), a list-valued local indexed by a literal (`th[0]`), an `if` EXPRESSION in integer position (`rho(0..if slot == SC_DMM { lf } else { ld })`), a local sliced to a prefix (`fixed(&r_h[..lkv])`), an integer-valued `let`, and a tuple-match arm whose value is an integer expression.  Every substituted value is the toy's and comes from B-7's profile; no count, row or plane is assumed.

B-10  `define`'s preamble is outside the parsed region.  The committed `parse()` runs the `match slot` arms only, and the shape generalisation moved the axis logs, the byte-limb counts and the pad-rule flags into a preamble above that match (argument.rs:873-891).  ADAPTER: `BlockDefineParser._statement` binds those eleven locals into each arm's environment at the toy's values before the first statement runs -- `lt` / `lh` / `ldh` / `ld` / `lf` / `lkv` from B-7's axis logs, `ln` / `ls` / `lp` from B-7's limb counts, and `pad_on = false` / `n_pad = 0`, which is what `Shape::toy()` gives: `pad.rs:365-368` returns no zero-rule plane unless `Shape::carries_pad_rule` (`shape.rs:360-362` is `!is_frozen_toy`, `shape.rs:367-369` is `profile == TOY_PROFILE`), so `define`'s `pad_doms` is empty, ruling P-1's pad term is absent and `B::supp` (argument.rs:543-547) returns `None` on every domain.  The pad branches this switches off contain no site call at all, so the committed `_run_arm`'s own `consumed == expected_calls` check still covers every site the arm makes.
caveat: These verdicts are about a LINEAR-ALGEBRA MODEL of the real Rust schedule of hashline/src/private_block/, at seeded stand-in challenges. The models exclude the sampled columns, the salted Merkle paths, the CFS channel, transcript conditioning, integer-range side information and correlation between A and H -- exactly as on the accepted attention layout (ZK60_PRIVATE_ATTENTION_NATIVE.md:79). NOTHING here establishes a privacy property of the construction: the joint-view gate on captured receipts is unmet and D8 / D11 stay open for the block's two external endpoints x_in and xres2. What is new relative to the paper runs is only that the schedule is now READ OUT OF CODE instead of out of a memo.
